videos.title: How to determine if a sequence is arithmetic or geometric
videos.description:
👉 Learn how to determine if a sequence is arithmetic, geometric, or neither. A sequence is a list of numbers/values exhibiting a defined pattern. A number/value in a sequence is called a term of the sequence. There are many types of sequence, among which are: arithmetic and geometric sequence. 

An arithmetic sequence is a sequence in which each term of the sequence is obtained by adding a common value, called the common difference, to the preceding term. A geometric sequence is a sequence in which each term of the sequence is obtained by multiplying/dividing by a common value, called the common ratio, to the preceding term.

Given a sequence, we can determine whether the sequence is arithmetic, geometric, or neither by comparing the terms of the sequence. If each term of the sequence is obtained by adding/subtracting a common value to/from the preceding term, then the sequence is an arithmetic sequence. If each term of the sequence is obtained by multiplying the preceding term with or dividing the preceding term by a common value, then the sequence is a geometric sequence. If none of the two conditions were met, then the sequence is neither an arithmetic or a geometric sequence.

The formula for the nth term of an arithmetic sequence is given by An = a + (n - 1)d, where a is the first term, n is the term number and d is the common difference. We can obtain the common difference by subtracting a term from the succeeding term or if the known terms are not consecutive, we can obtain the common difference by dividing the difference of the two terms by the difference of their term numbers. Plugging the required values into the formula, we can obtain the required nth term of the arithmetic sequence.

More Lessons: http://www.MathAndScience.com
Twitter: https://twitter.com/JasonGibsonMath


In this lesson, you will learn what an arithmetic sequence is in math and how it compares to the geometric sequence.  In an arithmetic sequence, each term of the sequence is related by a common difference.  That is, the arithmetic sequence formula dictates that the next term in the sequence is calculated by adding a constant value to the previous term.  In this way, if you one subtracts any two adjacent terms in the sequence, the same common difference will arise between terms.  We will discuss how to solve problems that involve the arithmetic sequence.

videos.title: 07 - The Geometric Sequence - Definition & Meaning - Part 1
videos.description:
More Lessons: http://www.MathAndScience.com
Twitter: https://twitter.com/JasonGibsonMath

  In this lesson, we will learn about the concept of a geometric sequence.  A geometric sequence in math is a list, or sequence, of numbers where each term is calculated by taking the previous term and multiplying by a constant number.  For example if we start with a known first term, we could find the second term by multiplying by 2.  The third term could then be found by multiplying the second term by 2, and so on.  Because of this, every term is related to the previous term in the sequence by a constant multiple.  This is usually described by saying that each pair of terms is related by a common ratio.  Geometric sequences are usually introduced in Algebra, but find most of their uses in pre-calculus and calculus.  In calculus, we use the geometric sequence and the related geometric series quite often when determining if and when a series converges.  Finally, the geometric sequence is related to the arithmetic sequence, where each term differs by a common difference.  That is, in an arithmetic sequence, each subsequent term is found by taking the previous term and adding or subtracting a constant number.

videos.title: What is arithmetic sequences and how do we determine them
videos.description:
👉 Learn how to determine if a sequence is arithmetic, geometric, or neither. A sequence is a list of numbers/values exhibiting a defined pattern. A number/value in a sequence is called a term of the sequence. There are many types of sequence, among which are: arithmetic and geometric sequence. 

An arithmetic sequence is a sequence in which each term of the sequence is obtained by adding a common value, called the common difference, to the preceding term. A geometric sequence is a sequence in which each term of the sequence is obtained by multiplying/dividing by a common value, called the common ratio, to the preceding term.

Given a sequence, we can determine whether the sequence is arithmetic, geometric, or neither by comparing the terms of the sequence. If each term of the sequence is obtained by adding/subtracting a common value to/from the preceding term, then the sequence is an arithmetic sequence. If each term of the sequence is obtained by multiplying the preceding term with or dividing the preceding term by a common value, then the sequence is a geometric sequence. If none of the two conditions were met, then the sequence is neither an arithmetic or a geometric sequence.

videos.title: The Bernoulli Principle is WILD.
videos.description:
Bernoulli’s Principle is a fascinating concept in fluid dynamics that helps explain how airplanes fly, why a curveball curves, and even how your shower curtain can mysteriously pull inward when the water's running. The principle states that as the speed of a fluid (like air or water) increases, its pressure decreases. This may seem counterintuitive at first, but it's the secret behind a lot of everyday phenomena.

Take an airplane wing, for example. The wing is designed so that air moves faster over the top than underneath. According to Bernoulli’s Principle, the faster-moving air on top has lower pressure, while the slower air beneath has higher pressure. This difference in pressure creates lift, allowing the plane to take off and stay in the air.

The same principle can be seen when you blow between two sheets of paper and watch them move closer together—the air speed between the sheets increases, causing a pressure drop and drawing them inward. From sports to aerodynamics, Bernoulli’s Principle is at work all around us, offering a simple yet powerful explanation for the behavior of fluids and the forces they create in motion. It’s a fundamental concept that brings a new perspective to the world of physics!

videos.title: The Physics of the Bernoulli Effect
videos.description:
Bernoulli's Principle is a cornerstone of fluid dynamics, revealing the fascinating relationship between a fluid's speed, pressure, and potential energy. Named after Swiss mathematician Daniel Bernoulli, this principle states that as the speed of a fluid increases, its pressure decreases.

Imagine blowing over the top of a sheet of paper—it rises! This simple demonstration showcases Bernoulli’s magic in action. When air moves faster over the paper, the pressure above it drops, while the higher pressure beneath pushes it upward.

This principle is critical in explaining how airplanes soar. Air travels faster over the curved top of a wing than beneath the flatter bottom. The pressure difference creates lift, allowing massive planes to defy gravity and fly. It’s not just about flight, though! Bernoulli’s Principle governs the flow of liquids through pipes, the curve of a soccer ball, and even the efficiency of venturi meters in measuring fluid flow.

From engineering marvels to everyday phenomena, Bernoulli’s Principle is a testament to the elegance of physics. It reminds us that understanding how forces interact with fluids unlocks countless innovations, bridging science and real-world wonders.

videos.title: Exploring Marshmallows Microscopically
videos.description:
Looking at marshmallows under a microscope turns a simple snack into a world of scientific wonder! Beneath their fluffy exterior lies a fascinating microstructure that reveals the secrets of their squishy, light-as-air nature. Marshmallows are made up of a delicate network of sugar, gelatin, and tiny air pockets. This combination gives them their signature texture and makes them a perfect subject for exploring material science and food chemistry.

Under magnification, you’ll see the intricate web of gelatin proteins that act like a flexible scaffold, holding everything together. These proteins trap millions of minuscule air bubbles, creating the soft, spongy structure we love. The sugar forms a crystalline structure that adds sweetness while contributing to the marshmallow’s stability.

This microscopic exploration offers valuable lessons about aeration, elasticity, and structural integrity. It’s not just a snack—it’s a teaching tool for understanding how food engineers and scientists design textures in everything from marshmallows to mousse.

Beyond the science, examining marshmallows this closely fosters curiosity and creativity. Who knew that such a common treat held such extraordinary secrets? Whether you’re a student, a food scientist, or just a curious mind, marshmallows under the microscope provide a sweet lens into the microscopic world.
